capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because Essential Utilities files its capital expenditures on the cash-flow line 'Property, plant and equipment additions' tagged us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings, which is not in the engine's candidate tag list (the engine's PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment series ends at FY2018). Filed values in the FY2025 10-K: $1,199,103,000 (FY2023), $1,329,747,000 (FY2024), $1,429,980,000 (FY2025). The engine applies this single value to every missing period; the value used is the median of the three filed years (the FY2024 figure). Against the true per-year figures it overstates FY2023 capex by $130,644,000 (conservative direction — lowers that year's OE) and understates FY2025 capex by $100,233,000 (flatters the latest year — noted, not hidden; the verdict does not change on the true figures, since OCF minus capex minus SBC is negative in all three years either way). Excluded, deliberately: 'Acquisitions of utility systems, net' ($57,004,000 in FY2025, same statement) is system M&A presented separately by the filer, not capex.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0000078128-26-000050), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Property, plant and equipment additions, including the debt component of allowance for funds used during construction': $(1,429,980) thousand for FY2025, $(1,329,747) thousand for FY2024 and $(1,199,103) thousand for FY2023; the identical three figures are reported as consolidated capital expenditures in the same 10-K's segment note (Note 19) and are tagged in EDGAR companyfacts under us-gaap PaymentsToAcquireBuildings. The override value is the median of the three filed years.

moat_against: Returns are set by regulators, not the company — allowed ROE caps the economics and ROIC has run only ~4-6%
Capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — growth is funded with debt and ATM equity issuance, diluting per-share economics
Gas segment faces long-run electrification / decarbonization transition risk
PFAS and water-quality mandates force capex whose recovery depends on rate-case outcomes
Pending American Water merger adds approval and integration risk; standalone moat is being absorbed into AWK's
moat_for: Exclusive regulated service territories — legal monopoly on water/wastewater for ~5.5 million people across nine states
Essential, non-discretionary service with inelastic demand and a proven regulatory-recovery mechanism for infrastructure spend
Rate-base model: $1.7B of 2026 infrastructure investment enters rate base and earns an allowed return, compounding regulated earnings
Scale as one of the largest U.S. water/wastewater utilities, with an acquisition pipeline of municipal systems
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated territories and essential-service demand make the franchise durable, but regulators cap the return on it: roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) ran 4.3% / 4.4% / 4.3% / 4.4% / 6.1% over FY2021-FY2025 — at or below a normal cost of capital — and gross margin is not filed (the company reports no COGS split). That is a moderate moat (5/10): the moat protects volume and recovery, not price. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 5 = 8.5 years.
name: Essential Utilities, Inc.
one_liner: Durable regulated water/gas monopoly (moat 5/10) whose capex structurally exceeds operating cash flow — conservative owner's earnings are negative in every recent year, so it cannot clear the 15% hurdle on this model at any plausible price; the live investment question is the pending all-stock American Water merger (0.305 AWK shares per WTRG share, expected to close by end of Q1 2027), not standalone DCF value.
